transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess what brought me in is I kind of went from just being one of the normal guys on the landscaping crew to suddenly trying to run everything, like three different bids at once, calling city people, trying to line up plant suppliers, messaging everybody I knew about this park idea I had.

And it’s not like me, usually. I mean, I’ll work hard, sure, but this was like I couldn’t shut it off. I’d be thinking about mulch pricing and permits and who has native grasses, and then I’d remember this park near my aunt’s place that’s always got trash by the fence—sorry, that’s not really the point. The point is I got really wrapped up in it, like way more than made sense, and people started telling me I needed to talk to somebody.
During this time, did you feel like you needed much less sleep than usual?

I don’t know… I mean, I wasn’t really tracking it like that. Some nights I’d be up thinking about stuff, but I can’t say if it was less sleep or just my normal bad schedule, you know? Landscaping hours get weird depending on the job, and if we’ve got an early start I’m already kind of—sorry, I’m not sure. I didn’t really notice it as “I don’t need sleep,” if that’s what you mean.
During that time, did you feel unusually important or especially capable, like you could take on much more than other people?

Yeah… I mean, yeah, I guess I did. At the time it didn’t feel crazy to me, it felt like I was just finally seeing the bigger picture.

Like I honestly thought I was about to be the guy every town around here would call for sustainable landscaping. Not just our usual little jobs, but parks, medians, city projects, all that. And I’m saying that while I’m still trying to keep my own small jobs paid up, you know? Like I don’t even have everything steady, but I was talking like I was already running some big operation.
During that time, did you believe things that other people said weren’t true or out of touch with reality?

I’m not sure. I mean, people definitely said I was getting carried away, or that I was talking like things were already set when they weren’t. But as far as, like, believing something totally not real… I don’t know.

I was convinced the park thing could happen, but then again, parks do get redone, you know? They put in those little rain gardens by the library a couple towns over, and everybody acted like that was some genius idea when it’s basically just choosing the right plants and grading it so the water goes where it should—sorry. I guess I’m saying I don’t know if it was “out of touch with reality” or just me being way too sure of myself.
Did this period cause serious problems at work or in your relationships?

Yeah… I mean, it’s starting to, I think. Work especially.

I’ve been missing little details on bids, like measurements or materials, stuff I usually catch. And with landscaping, a “little detail” can turn into a whole mess, because if you order wrong or grade something wrong, then water goes where it shouldn’t, or someone’s using equipment based on a bad plan. I keep thinking one bad mistake could cost me clients—or worse, get somebody hurt on a job site.

Relationships… I don’t know. Work is the one I notice most.
During this time, did you hear voices or sounds that other people could not hear?

Not that I can really say. I mean, sometimes on job sites there’s always noise—mowers, trailers rattling, somebody yelling from the other side of a yard—and I’ll think I heard something, but then it’s just… you know, normal noise.

I don’t think I was hearing voices that nobody else could hear. Nothing like that stands out to me.
Have you ever had a period in your life when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Yeah… yeah, I have. It’s been kind of hanging over me for, I don’t know, about a year now. Not every single minute, but most days it’s there, like this weight I wake up with.

And lately it’s gotten worse—this last crash, or whatever you’d call it, is the worst it’s been. I keep thinking maybe it’ll lift if I just get through the week, like when weather delays a job and you’re just waiting for the ground to dry out, but it hasn’t really been like that. It’s just been… there.
About how long did that unusually energized, driven period last?

About two weeks, I think. It kind of started when I got it in my head that I was going to remake myself for that park pitch—you know, really prove I could handle something bigger than the usual jobs.

I got all fired up and overconfident, like I had this whole new version of myself mapped out. And then after maybe two weeks of that… I just crashed.
During that energized two-week period, did your behavior become so severe that you had to be hospitalized or that you couldn’t keep functioning at work?

The work part is where it started getting scary. I mean, I was still trying to handle jobs, but I’d catch myself missing details on bids or measurements—stuff I normally double-check without even thinking.

And in landscaping, one wrong measurement or missed detail can turn into a real mess. Like, it’s not just paperwork, you know? It can cost me a client, or if something’s off on a job site, somebody could get hurt. So I wouldn’t say it was just “extra energy” helping me. It was starting to mess with how I work.
During that energized period, did you ever feel completely certain of something that other people said was impossible or clearly untrue?

Yeah… I mean, not like I thought I could fly or something. But I was really, really sure I was about to become the guy every town around here would call for sustainable landscaping.

Like, in my head it wasn’t even a maybe. I was picturing city people, parks departments, everybody wanting me specifically—even though realistically I’m still just trying to keep my smaller jobs paid up and make sure the truck doesn’t need some repair I can’t afford.

I remember talking like it was already happening, like I’d cracked some code nobody else had. And if someone kind of hinted that it was a lot to assume, I’d just think they didn’t get it.
During that energized period, did your behavior seriously damage any friendships, family relationships, or create major conflicts with other people?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if I’d call it “seriously damaged,” like nobody stopped speaking to me forever or anything, but I definitely caused conflict.

Before I crashed, I felt so fired up—almost like bigger than myself, if that makes sense—and if one of the guys at work questioned the plan or told me to slow down, I’d snap at him way harder than made sense. Like he’d just be saying, “Maybe we should measure that again,” and I’d take it like he was doubting me personally.

And then I’d be mad about it for way too long, even though normally I can let that stuff go. I guess it did make things tense. I wasn’t easy to be around.
During that energized period, did you ever believe you had a special power, identity, or mission that other people clearly said wasn’t real?

I don’t know if I’d call it a special power exactly… like I wasn’t saying I had some magic thing. But I did feel like I had this mission, kind of, like I was supposed to be the person who changed how landscaping got done around here.

I honestly believed I was about to become the guy every town around here called for sustainable landscaping. Like parks, city jobs, all of it. And I’d talk about it like it was basically already set, even though, if I’m being honest, I’m still just trying to keep my small jobs paid up and not fall behind on the regular stuff.

It sounds kind of embarrassing saying it out loud now. At the time it felt obvious to me, like everyone else just hadn’t caught up yet.
